datapoint.context: ists expect the unemployment rate climbed to 9.7 percent last month from 9

qk_vs_ov_reading: mlp1 dominates yet again (6.48 nats, ~180x the top head) -- even numeric-formatting continuations (predicting '.' to complete a truncated decimal '9' echoing the earlier '9.7') are mostly resolved by the token-table. Both top heads are cleanly in the SELECTION regime: 10.0 (qk=0.0373 ~ ov=0.035) and 1.4 (qk=0.0285 ~ ov=0.0302) -- ablating their attention pattern hurts almost as much as ablating their output, meaning WHERE they look (plausibly back to the earlier '9.7') matters more than any special payload content.
category_story: Consistent with DP1/DP2: mlp1 removal devastates the same broad class (subword continuations + fixed templates) across 94% of all positions; this decimal-point datapoint is just one more instance the giant token-table happens to cover, not evidence of a numeric-specific submodule.
surprises: This is the one datapoint where BOTH top heads are unambiguously selection-driven (qk~ov) rather than payload-driven -- suggesting decimal/number-echo prediction leans on copy-by-attention (finding the earlier occurrence of the number) more than the acronym or phrasal datapoints did, even though the overall CE is still owned by mlp1.
